definitions.explanation: An involuntary spasm of the diaphragm that causes a sudden intake of breath, producing a characteristic sound.

examples.japanese: しゃっくりが{止|と}まらない。
{水|みず}を{飲|の}んだらしゃっくりが{止|と}まった。
examples.english: The hiccups stopped after I drank some water.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで{食|た}べたらしゃっくりが{出|で}た。
examples.english: I got hiccups because I ate too quickly.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}{中|ちゅう}にしゃっくりが{止|と}まらなくなって、{息|いき}を{止|と}めてみたら{少|すこ}し{良|よ}くなった。
examples.english: I couldn't stop hiccupping during a meeting, and it got a little better when I tried holding my breath.

notes:
しゃっくり refers to hiccups — the involuntary spasm that causes a sudden intake of breath. Can be used as a する verb: しゃっくりする (to hiccup).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- しゃっくりが{出|で}る: to get the hiccups
- しゃっくりが{止|と}まる: hiccups stop
- しゃっくりが{止|と}まらない: can't stop hiccupping
- しゃっくりを{止|と}める: to stop hiccups (intentionally)

FOLK REMEDIES:
Japan has similar folk remedies to English-speaking countries:
- {水|みず}を{飲|の}む: drinking water
- {息|いき}を{止|と}める: holding one's breath
- {驚|おどろ}かせる: startling/surprising someone

ALTERNATE FORMS:
Also written as しゃっくり or ひゃっくり. The kanji form {吃逆|しゃっくり} exists but is rarely used.
